headline: DuckDuckGo survey reveals users share sensitive info with AI chatbots
summary: A new survey by DuckDuckGo highlights the extent to which individuals are disclosing personal data to AI tools like ChatGPT, raising privacy concerns.
details: A recent survey conducted by DuckDuckGo indicates that a significant number of users are sharing personal information with AI chatbots. The findings shed light on potential privacy risks associated with the increasing use of these advanced AI tools.

The survey, which focused on user interactions with AI like ChatGPT, revealed that many individuals are not fully aware of the data they are disclosing. This includes sensitive details that could be misused if not properly protected.

These findings underscore the need for greater user education and robust privacy measures from AI developers. As AI becomes more integrated into daily life, understanding the implications of data sharing is crucial for protecting personal information.

headline_marked: Nvidia Vera CPU: [[88 cores]] with spatial multithreading, 1.2 TB/s memory
headline: Nvidia Vera CPU: 88 cores with spatial multithreading, 1.2 TB/s memory
summary: Nvidia details its next-gen Vera CPU, designed for agentic AI workloads, featuring a novel spatial multithreading approach and high-speed memory.
details: Nvidia has unveiled more details about its upcoming Vera CPU at Hot Chips 2026, highlighting its design for agentic AI workloads. Vera is Nvidia's first CPU with a custom core, moving away from the stock Arm design used in Grace. It will be available as a single 88-core SKU.

A key innovation in Vera is its 'spatial multithreading' implementation, which Nvidia claims reduces the performance impact of other threads running on the same core. This differs from traditional Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) by managing resource contention more deterministically, leading to more consistent per-core performance.

Nvidia has benchmarked Vera against AMD's EPYC 9655P, showing a 24% speed increase in browser instance scaling for agentic workloads. The company also demonstrated Vera compiling the Linux kernel 22% faster for native AArch64 targets and 14% faster for x86 cross-compilation.

The Vera CPU boasts a monolithic compute die and an LPDDR5X memory subsystem, capable of delivering up to 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth. This high bandwidth is crucial for handling the complex and demanding nature of agentic AI tasks, which Nvidia describes as 'the most complex computing workload in history'.

Nvidia's agentic AI focus is evident in its approach to benchmarks. For browser tasks, agents can operate up to 4.5x faster by omitting elements like GUI rendering and media decoding. Code compilation is also a key metric, with Vera showing significant gains over its competitors.
